messages.content:
You are formalising an English argument into Verifiable English (VE), a small
first-order logic with a checker. You receive the argument split into
numbered SENTENCES, each with a role:
- given: the text states it as a premise (declared rules, records, facts);
- claimed: the argument asserts it as a conclusion; it must be derived;
- context: needs nothing.
TARGET sentences are the argument's final conclusion(s).

What a finished formalisation contains:
1. The frozen TARGET: the formal statement of each target sentence, written
   first and never changed afterwards.
2. NODES. Each node is ONE VE statement anchored to the sentence id(s) it
   formalises. A node without parents is an assumption; an assumption must be
   anchored to a GIVEN sentence that states it. A node with parents is a step:
   it must follow logically from its parents, and the checker certifies this
   (or returns a countermodel: a situation where every parent is true and the
   step is false).
3. COVERAGE: every asserting sentence (given or claimed) is covered by a node
   anchored to it, or explicitly waived with a reason (e.g. a sentence that only
   says which rules are declared, or a fact the argument never uses).
4. A certified chain from anchored assumptions to a step that states each
   frozen target exactly.

Fidelity is your responsibility and is audited independently, sentence by
sentence: each node must say what its sentence says, no more and no less.
Give every claimed sentence its OWN step node stating exactly what that
sentence concludes (with that sentence's reasons as parents); do not skip
intermediate conclusions or anchor one node to several sentences it does not
fully state. Where a word has several
senses (several predicates), the given sentences name the sense; a claimed
sentence may leave it open. Then choose the sense that the sentence's own
stated reasons (and the given records they rely on) actually establish. Do
not switch to another sense just because a later step needs it; a step that
needs a different sense of the same word is a gap. Never add a premise that
no given sentence states: an unanchored assumption that a certified step
depends on fails the item. The argument itself MAY be flawed. If a claimed
step does not follow when faithfully formalised, do not force it: leave it
unproved and finish with verdict "gap", naming the step node(s).

VE strict syntax (exact spacing and parentheses; every compound operand is parenthesised):
  F ::= true | false
      | T is UNARY                      e.g. @pebble is marked
      | T BINARY T                      e.g. @lot1 supplied @pebble
      | T equals T
      | not (F)
      | (F) and (F)      | (F) or (F)   binary only: (A) and ((B) and (C))
      | if (F), then (F)
      | for every SORT v, (F)  | there exists SORT v, (F)
  T ::= variable | @constant
Examples (unrelated vocabulary, do not copy symbols):
  if ((@pebble is marked) and (@pebble is round)), then (@stone is marked).
  for every rock r, (if (r is marked), then (r is round)).
Never add extra parentheses: each operand gets exactly one pair, e.g.
  if ((@a is p) and (@b is q)), then (@c is r).   not   if (((@a is p) and (@b is q))), then ((@c is r)).
Use ONLY the sorts, predicates and constants listed in the materials.
Constants are written with @ (e.g. @unit5). A statement ends with a period.
A step's parents are node names; a rule node (an 'if ... then' assumption)
must be listed as a parent of any step that uses it.

You have no interactive tools. Each turn, write the COMPLETE formalisation as
one JSON document (format below). The harness freezes your targets from your
first document (they cannot change later), adds every node, runs the checker
on every step and returns diagnostics: parse errors, per-step results
(follows / countermodel with the model / unknown), unanchored assumptions and
uncovered sentences. Then write a corrected COMPLETE document. The session
ends when a document passes every check, when you include "finish", or when
the budget runs out.

Document format (JSON, no comments):
{"targets": {"<target id>": "<VE statement>"},
 "nodes": [{"name": "<[a-z][a-z0-9_]*>", "text": "<VE statement>",
            "anchors": ["<sentence id>", ...], "parents": ["<node name>", ...]}],
 "waivers": {"<sentence id>": "<reason>"},
 "finish": {"verdict": "complete" | "gap", "gap_steps": ["<node>"], "note": "..."}}
"finish" is optional; include it only when you are done.

SENTENCES (id [role] text):
  n05.1 [given] Rules r00, r14, r12, r05 are declared.
  n06.1 [given] Rules r03, r07, r08 are declared.
  n19.1 [given] Rules r06, r10, r13 are declared.

  r14.1 [given] If unit3 is sound (casing intact), then unit3 is sound (signal audible).
  r10.1 [given] If unit5 is sound (signal audible), then unit5 is logged.
  n18.1 [claimed] Because unit5 is bundled and unit5 is retained and unit5 is packed, unit3 is ready.
  n18.2 [claimed] The checks that unit5 is stacked and unit5 is checked and unit5 is coded would imply that unit1 is stable and unit1 is stable and unit5 is stable, respectively.
  n07.1 [claimed] Since unit5 is mounted and unit5 is routed and unit5 is rated, it follows that unit3 is ready.
  n03.1 [claimed] Given that unit3 is ready and unit3 is ready, we infer that unit5 is ready.
  n08.1 [claimed] It follows that unit5 is weighed-in because unit3 is ready and the immediately preceding ready result holds.
  n16.1 [claimed] Because unit5 is weighed-in, unit3 is sound.
  n12.1 [claimed] Since unit3 is sound, it follows that unit3 is sound.
  n04.1 [claimed] Given that unit3 is sound, we infer that unit5 is sound.
  n20.1 [claimed] It follows that unit5 is logged because the immediately preceding sound result holds.
  n10.1 [claimed] Because unit5 is logged, unit3 is cleared.
  n02.1 [claimed] Since unit3 is cleared, it follows that unit3 is cleared.
  n17.1 [claimed] Given that unit3 is cleared, we infer that unit1 is cleared.
  n00.1 [claimed] It follows that unit5 is balanced because the immediately preceding cleared result holds.
  n13.1 [claimed] Because unit5 is balanced, unit3 is stable.
  n01.1 [claimed] Since unit3 is stable, it follows that unit3 is stable.
  n15.1 [claimed] Given that unit3 is stable and unit5 is scanned, we infer that unit5 is stable.
  n14.1 [claimed] It follows that unit5 is calibrated because the immediately preceding stable result holds.
TARGETS:
  t_n14 -> sentence n14.1: It follows that unit5 is calibrated because the immediately preceding stable result holds.
VOCABULARY:
  sorts: entity (A named dossier entity.)
  predicates (name(argument sorts): gloss):
    bagged(entity): bagged: bag fitted (R07)

messages.content:
You are formalising an English argument into Verifiable English (VE), a small
first-order logic with a checker. You receive the argument split into
numbered SENTENCES, each with a role:
- given: the text states it as a premise (declared rules, records, facts);
- claimed: the argument asserts it as a conclusion; it must be derived;
- context: needs nothing.
TARGET sentences are the argument's final conclusion(s).

What a finished formalisation contains:
1. The frozen TARGET: the formal statement of each target sentence, written
   first and never changed afterwards.
2. NODES. Each node is ONE VE statement anchored to the sentence id(s) it
   formalises. A node without parents is an assumption; an assumption must be
   anchored to a GIVEN sentence that states it. A node with parents is a step:
   it must follow logically from its parents, and the checker certifies this
   (or returns a countermodel: a situation where every parent is true and the
   step is false).
3. COVERAGE: every asserting sentence (given or claimed) is covered by a node
   anchored to it, or explicitly waived with a reason (e.g. a sentence that only
   says which rules are declared, or a fact the argument never uses).
4. A certified chain from anchored assumptions to a step that states each
   frozen target exactly.

Fidelity is your responsibility and is audited independently, sentence by
sentence: each node must say what its sentence says, no more and no less.
Give every claimed sentence its OWN step node stating exactly what that
sentence concludes (with that sentence's reasons as parents); do not skip
intermediate conclusions or anchor one node to several sentences it does not
fully state. Where a word has several
senses (several predicates), the given sentences name the sense; a claimed
sentence may leave it open. Then choose the sense that the sentence's own
stated reasons (and the given records they rely on) actually establish. Do
not switch to another sense just because a later step needs it; a step that
needs a different sense of the same word is a gap. Never add a premise that
no given sentence states: an unanchored assumption that a certified step
depends on fails the item. The argument itself MAY be flawed. If a claimed
step does not follow when faithfully formalised, do not force it: leave it
unproved and finish with verdict "gap", naming the step node(s).

VE strict syntax (exact spacing and parentheses; every compound operand is parenthesised):
  F ::= true | false
      | T is UNARY                      e.g. @pebble is marked
      | T BINARY T                      e.g. @lot1 supplied @pebble
      | T equals T
      | not (F)
      | (F) and (F)      | (F) or (F)   binary only: (A) and ((B) and (C))
      | if (F), then (F)
      | for every SORT v, (F)  | there exists SORT v, (F)
  T ::= variable | @constant
Examples (unrelated vocabulary, do not copy symbols):
  if ((@pebble is marked) and (@pebble is round)), then (@stone is marked).
  for every rock r, (if (r is marked), then (r is round)).
Never add extra parentheses: each operand gets exactly one pair, e.g.
  if ((@a is p) and (@b is q)), then (@c is r).   not   if (((@a is p) and (@b is q))), then ((@c is r)).
Use ONLY the sorts, predicates and constants listed in the materials.
Constants are written with @ (e.g. @unit5). A statement ends with a period.
A step's parents are node names; a rule node (an 'if ... then' assumption)
must be listed as a parent of any step that uses it.

You act through the tools listed below. Suggested order: freeze_target
for every target, then add assumption nodes for the given sentences you need,
then add step nodes for the claimed sentences with their parents and
check_step each one; waive sentences that need no formalisation; call status
to see what is still missing. When status reports success, or when you have
a faithful formalisation with a step you believe does not follow, call
finish. You may issue several tool calls per turn; they run in order.

tools.description: List the source sentences (id, role given/claimed/context), the targets, and the vocabulary (sorts, predicates with glosses, constants).
tools.name: sentences

tools.description: Commit the formal statement of a target sentence. Irreversible; must be done for every target before any node is added.
tools.name: freeze_target

surface.description: Input language: strict VE, the controlled English surface, or auto (strict first).

tools.description: Add one node (one VE statement). No parents = an assumption; with parents = a step that check_step must certify. Anchor it to the sentence id(s) it formalises. An assumption is anchored only by a 'given' sentence.
tools.name: add_node

parents.description: Existing node names this step follows from.

surface.description: Input language: strict VE, the controlled English surface, or auto (strict first).

text.description: One VE statement (omit to accept a candidate verbatim).

tools.description: Change a node's statement, anchors and/or parents. Invalidates its check and its children's checks.
tools.name: rewrite

surface.description: Input language: strict VE, the controlled English surface, or auto (strict first).

tools.description: Remove a node that is not a parent of another node.
tools.name: remove_node

tools.description: Declare a new predicate, constant or sort. A gloss (what it means) is required. Near-duplicates of existing vocabulary and names/glosses restating a target conclusion are blocked until acknowledged by flag.
tools.name: declare

acknowledge.description: Flags from a blocked declaration you accept.

verbalisation.description: Optional English template, e.g. '{0} is sealed'.

tools.description: Check whether a step follows from its parents. Returns 'follows' (a replayed certificate), 'countermodel' (a checked model where every parent is true and the conclusion false), or 'unknown'.
tools.name: check_step

tools.description: Summarise progress: target certification (graph replay), unproved steps, unanchored assumptions and whether they are load-bearing, sentence coverage/waivers, renamed-conclusion flags, provenance counts and token usage. 'success' is true only when everything passes.
tools.name: status

tools.description: Explicitly mark an asserting sentence as not needing formalisation, with a reason.
tools.name: waive

tools.description: Show all nodes (or one node, with history) with their deterministic English paraphrase.
tools.name: show

tools.description: Parse a VE statement without adding it; return canonical text and paraphrase.
tools.name: paraphrase

surface.description: Input language: strict VE, the controlled English surface, or auto (strict first).

tools.description: Compare two statements (node names, target ids, candidate ids, or VE text): equivalent / a_stronger / b_stronger / incomparable, with checked distinguishing models.
tools.name: compare

tools.description: End the session. verdict 'complete' when status reports success; 'gap' when your faithful formalisation has step(s) that do not follow (name them in gap_steps).
tools.name: finish
